evidence.caption: Where it begins. Not where it ends.

authorNotes.meaning: Pure atmosphere: misty hills and a loch fit Excalibur, Conan, any sword myth. It is Glenfinnan country — where the story starts in 1536. The caption is the whole game in eight words: this story does not stay here.

Four and a half centuries in one film. Conan and Excalibur die here — both live entirely in their ancient worlds. And the trap springs organically: two eras in one story makes players reach for The Terminator, whose time-jump is the most famous in cinema.

The designed trap. Players who know their Queen jump to Flash Gordon — the band's famous 1980 score — and they're not wrong about the history, only the film: Queen scored BOTH movies on this board. 'Princes of the Universe,' 'Who Wants to Live Forever.' The Princess Bride dies quietly here (Mark Knopfler, no Queen).

evidence.content: THE SCOTSMAN WAS PLAYED BY A FRENCHMAN. HIS EGYPTIAN MENTOR — BY A SCOT.

authorNotes.meaning: The most gloriously backwards casting of the decade: Christopher Lambert, a Frenchman, as the Highlander; Sean Connery, Scotland itself, as Juan Sánchez-Villalobos Ramírez, an Egyptian posing as a Spaniard. No such absurdity exists in The Terminator — it dies here.

evidence.content: ITS DIRECTOR MADE THE FIRST MUSIC VIDEO EVER PLAYED ON MTV
evidence.caption: August 1, 1981, 12:01 a.m.

authorNotes.meaning: Russell Mulcahy directed 'Video Killed the Radio Star' — the video that launched MTV — and brought that exact visual grammar to the film. Flash Gordon (directed by Mike Hodges, no music-video history) finally dies, and the trap is fully broken.

The smoking gun: six words that everyone has heard, whether or not they know where from. One search settles it — and the reveal gets to enjoy the irony that a film about there being only one spawned four sequels and a TV series.

reveal.summary: Highlander. It opens in the misty glens of 1536 Scotland and ends in a 1985 New York parking garage, because Connor MacLeod cannot die. Queen wrote the soundtrack — 'Princes of the Universe,' and 'Who Wants to Live Forever' for the century-crossing love story — six years after scoring the other film on this board, Flash Gordon. The casting was gloriously backwards: Frenchman Christopher Lambert as the Scot, Sean Connery as the Egyptian mentor with the Edinburgh accent. Director Russell Mulcahy had made 'Video Killed the Radio Star,' the first video MTV ever aired, and shot the film like the world's longest, best music video. It flopped in theaters, conquered video stores, and its six-word tagline outgrew the movie: there can be only one — followed, inevitably, by four sequels and a television series.
reveal.evidenceToAnswer: The funnel: the glen fits every sword myth on the board; the 1536→1985 span kills the single-era epics while luring you toward The Terminator; the Queen soundtrack is a fair trap — the band really did score Flash Gordon too; the backwards casting belongs to no other film; the MTV-director fact finishes Flash Gordon; and the six-word tagline can only be one thing.
